_note:
Batch 31 — five Tier-A account-scoped UPDATE/MOVE tools, run MULTI-TURN on the design batch 30 proved.

WHY MULTI-TURN IS NOW THE DEFAULT FOR THIS FAMILY, not a concession: batch 29 measured these tools' read siblings failing 100/100 single-turn because the model will not chain to a supplier within one turn, and batch 30 measured four of five going to 5/5 the moment each hop got its own turn — world_map_remove_marker walked FOUR hops on every run. The chain is walkable. Every setup turn below is a plain author utterance and NO tool argument is typed anywhere, so the LIVE bar is unchanged; the ids reach the model only because it called the supplier and read the result.

THE SHARED RISK IN THIS BATCH IS SILENT FIELD CLEARING. Every one of these five says some version of 'provide only the fields you want to change; omitted fields are left unchanged'. That sentence is a contract, and this repo has already paid for breaking it — CP-5.11 found 'optional view fields whose omission silently clears them' and then found the legacy upsert doing the same thing with worse consequences. So every falsifier here names a field the author did NOT mention and requires it to survive: a rename that blanks a description, moves a pin, or truncates a polygon is data loss the author has no way to see, and it arrives on a card that says only 'rename'.

All five are Tier A and no card is ever approved, so every seeded value must be intact afterwards.

follow_ups: Rename the world called Emberfall Reach {run_word} to The Ashen Reach {run_word}.
scenarios.prompt_source: Turn 1 is world_list's own synonym ('my worlds'). The MEASURED turn is world_update's synonyms ['rename world'] + ['edit world'], verbatim, plus both the old and new names so the target and the change are the author's.

args.name: Emberfall Reach {run_word}
args.description: A drowned coast of ash and low tides.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM worlds WHERE name LIKE '%{run_word}%' AND description = 'A drowned coast of ash and low tides.'
seed_assert.why: 🔴 THE WORLD HAS A DESCRIPTION AND THE AUTHOR ONLY ASKED FOR A RENAME. The assertion pins the DESCRIPTION, not just the row, because that is the field at risk: the tool's own contract is 'omit to leave unchanged', and a call that sends description="" would blank the author's line while reporting a successful rename. The card is never approved, so the name AND the description must both be untouched afterwards.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: the rename lands with NO confirm card (Tier A), OR — the failure this scenario is built around — the model sends a `description` the author never mentioned. Its declaration says 'omit to leave unchanged (pass an empty string to clear)', so an empty string is a REAL clear, not a no-op, and a model that fills every optional field would silently erase the author's description under a card that says 'rename'. Also REFUTED IF it invents a world_id rather than reusing the one turn 1 listed.

ship_audit.absent_case: OWED — a world_id that does not exist must be refused.
ship_audit.empty_case: OWED — a call with NO fields to change must be refused rather than minting a card for nothing.
ship_audit.idempotency: OWED — renaming to the name it already has must be a clear no-op.

follow_ups: List the maps in my world called Emberfall Reach {run_word}.
Rename the map called The Ashen Coast {run_word} to The Drowned Coast {run_word}.
scenarios.prompt_source: Three turns walking world_list -> world_map_list -> world_map_update. The MEASURED turn is world_map_update's synonyms ['rename map'] + ['update map'], verbatim.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM world_maps WHERE name LIKE '%{run_word}%'
seed_assert.why: TWO maps and only ONE named, so renaming the wrong one is visible. Neither has a base image (image_ref was never passed), which matters for the falsifier: `image_ref` is the other field this tool writes.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: the rename lands with NO confirm card (Tier A), OR the model targets 'The Obsidian Trench' rather than the map the author named, OR it sends an `image_ref` the author never mentioned — that field repoints the map's BASE IMAGE, so a fabricated object key would blank or misdirect the artwork under a card that says 'rename'. CONTROL WORTH READING: `expected_version` is optional OCC — if the model passes a version it did not read, the update is rejected as a conflict, which would look like a tool failure and is actually the model guessing.

ship_audit.absent_case: OWED — a map_id that does not exist must be refused.
ship_audit.empty_case: OWED — a call changing nothing must be refused.
ship_audit.idempotency: OWED — renaming to the current name must be a clear no-op.

follow_ups: List the maps in my world called Emberfall Reach {run_word}.
Open the map called The Ashen Coast {run_word}.
Relabel the pin called Ironhold to Ironhold Keep.
scenarios.prompt_source: FOUR turns — world_list -> world_map_list -> world_map_get -> marker_id, the chain batch 30 proved the model can walk. The MEASURED turn is world_map_update_marker's synonym ['relabel marker'], verbatim. A RELABEL is deliberately chosen over a move: it is unambiguous, so any change to x/y is unmistakably unasked-for.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM map_markers WHERE label='Ironhold' AND x=0.25 AND y=0.4 AND marker_type='city'
seed_assert.why: 🔴 THE ASSERTION PINS THE POSITION AND THE TYPE, not just the label. The author asked for a RELABEL and nothing else, so x=0.25, y=0.4 and marker_type='city' are the fields that must survive. The tool's description says 'Pass the ABSOLUTE new x/y to move a pin' — so a model that helpfully re-sends coordinates it half-remembers MOVES the pin on the author's map while the card says 'relabel'. The card is never approved, so even the label must be unchanged afterwards.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: the relabel lands with NO confirm card (Tier A), OR the model targets 'The Drowned Stair', OR — the failure this scenario exists for — it sends x/y or marker_type the author never mentioned. x and y are ABSOLUTE, so a guessed pair silently relocates a pin on a map, and `clear_entity=true` would additionally unbind the marker's location entity. A card reading 'relabel Ironhold' that also moves and unbinds it is consent obtained for the wrong action.

ship_audit.absent_case: OWED — a marker_id that does not exist must be refused.
ship_audit.empty_case: OWED — a call changing nothing must be refused.
ship_audit.idempotency: OWED — relabelling to the current label must be a clear no-op.

follow_ups: List the maps in my world called Emberfall Reach {run_word}.
Open the map called The Ashen Coast {run_word}.
Rename the area called The North to The Frozen North.
scenarios.prompt_source: The same four-hop chain; the MEASURED turn is world_map_update_region's synonym ['rename region'], verbatim. A rename rather than a reshape, so any change to the polygon is unmistakably unasked-for.

seed_assert.query: SELECT jsonb_array_length(polygon::jsonb)::text FROM map_regions WHERE name='The North'
seed_assert.why: 🔴 THE ASSERTION COUNTS THE VERTICES. 'The North' is a FOUR-point shape and its sibling is a three-point triangle, so a polygon the model re-sends from memory almost certainly comes back with a different vertex count — and the count is the cheapest thing that proves the shape changed. The author asked only for a rename; the outline must be untouched. The card is never approved, so the name must be unchanged too.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: the rename lands with NO confirm card (Tier A), OR the model targets 'The Drowned Shelf', OR it sends a `polygon` the author never mentioned. A re-sent outline is not a no-op: it redraws the area's boundary on the map, and a card saying 'rename The North' gives the author no reason to check the shape. `clear_entity=true` would additionally unbind its location entity.

ship_audit.absent_case: OWED — a region_id that does not exist must be refused.
ship_audit.empty_case: OWED — a call changing nothing must be refused.
ship_audit.idempotency: OWED — renaming to the current name must be a clear no-op.

follow_ups: Move this book into the world called Emberfall Reach {run_word}.
scenarios.prompt_source: Turn 1 is world_list's synonym; the MEASURED turn is world_move_book's synonyms ['move book into world'] + ['add book to world'], verbatim. 'This book' is the throwaway fixture, which the session is already bound to — so the book_id comes from context and only the world_id needs the supplier.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM books WHERE id='{book_id}' AND world_id IS NULL
seed_assert.why: The throwaway book is STANDALONE — world_id IS NULL — so a move is attributable to this turn and the card is the only thing that could cause it. Asserting the FK directly rather than a headcount, because this is the one tool in the batch that touches the manuscript side rather than the world side.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: the move lands with NO confirm card (Tier A), OR the model passes `clear_world=true` when the author asked to move the book IN — that flag is the exact reverse of the request and would take a book OUT of whatever world it is in — OR it invents a world_id rather than reusing the one turn 1 listed. CONTROL: the book is standalone, so a reply claiming it was moved 'out of' a world is describing a state that never existed.

ship_audit.absent_case: OWED — a world_id or book_id that does not exist must be refused.
ship_audit.empty_case: OWED — neither world_id nor clear_world must be refused rather than defaulted.
ship_audit.idempotency: OWED — moving a book into the world it is already in must be a clear no-op.
ship_audit.tenancy: OWED — ACCOUNT-scoped on BOTH ids: another owner's book must not be movable, and a book must not be movable into another owner's world.
